subject.title: feat: handle lifecycle slash commands natively in Windows chat

question: Should the Windows client adopt the other first-party clients’ native semantics for exact, attachment-free `/new`, `/reset`, and `/compact` inputs rather than sending those inputs to the chat model?
rationale: This is a new user-facing interaction contract, not only an internal repair: it intentionally intercepts previously model-bound slash text and adds gateway-session behavior to Windows chat.

options.title: Adopt native lifecycle parity
options.body: Land the exact-command behavior after conflict resolution and current-head proof confirms both gateway compatibility paths and reset confirmation semantics.

options.title: Keep model-routed slash text
options.body: Do not intercept lifecycle-looking input in Windows chat until a broader product decision establishes cross-client command semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt native lifecycle parity
recommendation.body: Land the exact-command behavior after conflict resolution and current-head proof confirms both gateway compatibility paths and reset confirmation semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the concrete implementation and can explain the intended parity contract while a current-main feature owner is identified during maintainer review.
